units.function: open by naming the job, then concede the difficulty, then name the answer

original_instantiations: What we built is meant to clear a crowded hall and to flag the spots that jam. The layout and the way people push on each other make that hard. What we offer is a plan that watches the whole building and still keeps each visitor.
The job of the plan is to empty the building and to point out where the flow stalls. The building and the crowd both fight that. So the plan has to see the whole and the person at once.

units.source_excerpt: The object of our model is to provide an emergency evacuation for the Louvre. In the meantime, this model can also identify potential bottlenecks and has certain adaptability. However, complex building structures and the interaction among people makes the problem much harder.
units.reusable_pattern: The object of our model is to [the job]. In the meantime, it can also [a second job]. However, [the difficulty] makes the problem much harder.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, first paragraph.
stable function: name the job, add a second, then concede the difficulty.
pattern: The object of our model is / In the meantime / However.
boundary: the difficulty must be real, not a flourish.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use the venue name.
Do not claim adaptability before showing an edit the model survives.

units.function: say where an effect lands, then name the two tools used for it

original_instantiations: Everything about a single person ends up in how fast the crowd moves. So when we work out that speed we use one rule for the open passages and another for the tight spots.
A person's effect shows up only as a change in the crowd's speed. For that speed we keep two rules, one for each kind of passage.

units.source_excerpt: The effect will be ultimately reflected in the flow speed of the crowd. In this way, while calculating the flow speed of the crowd, we adopt N&M model and Stable Evacuation Speed model to deal with different situation.
units.reusable_pattern: The effect will be ultimately reflected in [one quantity]. In this way, while calculating [that quantity], we adopt [tool A] and [tool B] to deal with different situation.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, second paragraph.
stable function: collapse many factors into one quantity, then name the tools.
pattern: ultimately reflected in / In this way, while calculating.
boundary: the quantity must really carry the factors.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not copy the model names.

units.function: name a simplification and claim it makes the rest easy

original_instantiations: We turn the building into a graph, then cut a many-to-many problem down to one start and one end by adding two made-up nodes. That one change makes everything after it far easier.
The building becomes a graph. Two extra nodes turn many starts and many ends into one of each. The rest of the work gets simpler because of it.

units.source_excerpt: The second part is to visualize the building into a graph. Then simplify the problem from muti-to-muti plan to single-to-single plan through adding two virtual nodes. This step makes the following solution much easier.
units.reusable_pattern: Then simplify the problem from [the hard form] to [the easy form] through [the device]. This step makes the following solution much easier.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, third paragraph.
stable function: sell a reduction by what it saves.
pattern: through adding / This step makes the following solution much easier.
boundary: say what the device actually removes.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a step easier without saying what it removed.

units.function: claim a method sees both the whole and the small

original_instantiations: With that, the method plans the routes from the point of view of the whole building and still keeps the small factors in.
Done this way, the plan looks at the building as one system and does not drop the detail.

units.source_excerpt: In this way, the algorithm can carry out route planning from the perspective of system, and fully consider the micro factors.
units.reusable_pattern: In this way, the algorithm can carry out [the job] from the perspective of [the whole], and fully consider [the small].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, fourth paragraph.
stable function: claim both scales at once.
pattern: from the perspective of / and fully consider.
boundary: both scales must appear later.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim both scales if only one is modeled.

units.function: give a runtime and a size, then hedge the match to reality

original_instantiations: On a made-up building the run finished in 0.457 seconds for 770 people. The outcome agrees with a real case, up to a point. It also clears the room in danger first, which is the part that matters.
A test building of 770 people was solved in under half a second. The result lines up with practice, partly. And the threatened room empties fastest.

units.source_excerpt: The model obtains the result within 0.457s with a scale of 770 people. Besides, to a certain extent, the result matches practical case. In addition, it is able to evacuate the crowd from the dangerous room with the fastest speed.
units.reusable_pattern: The model obtains the result within [time] with a scale of [number]. Besides, to a certain extent, the result matches [the check].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, fifth paragraph.
stable function: report speed, then soften the validation.
pattern: within / with a scale of / to a certain extent.
boundary: keep the hedge; do not upgrade it to proof.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the hedge.
Do not copy the numbers.

units.function: report the real case as a cost, a scale, an accuracy, and a total

original_instantiations: On the real building the run took 36.15 seconds for 6700 people, at a step of 0.1 seconds. The whole clearing took 288.7 seconds.
The full building, 6700 people, came back in 36.15 seconds at a tenth of a second. Clearing it took 288.7 seconds.

units.source_excerpt: Finally, we implement this model to the Louvre. It cost 36.15s to get the result with a scale of 6700 people and accuracy of 0.1s. The total evacuation cost 288.7s.
units.reusable_pattern: It cost [time] to get the result with a scale of [number] and accuracy of [step]. The total [outcome] cost [time].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, last paragraph.
stable function: stack the four numbers in one breath.
pattern: It cost / with a scale of / and accuracy of.
boundary: keep compute time separate from evacuation time.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge the two times.
Do not copy the numbers.

units.function: move from a trend to the need for one adaptable model

original_instantiations: Halls everywhere are paying more attention to getting people out and are hunting for a method that fits. So it is vital to build one model that travels well and bends to the case.
Venues are looking harder at safe exit and at methods that suit them. That makes one adaptable model worth building.

units.source_excerpt: Today, museums, libraries, and exhibition halls around the world are paying more attention to the safe evacuation of venues, and are looking for suitable emergency evacuation methods. Therefore, it is vital to establish a widely used and adaptable emergency evacuation model.
units.reusable_pattern: [The field] is paying more attention to [the problem], and looking for [a method]. Therefore, it is vital to establish [the model].
reusable_elements: occurrences: introduction, opening.
stable function: earn the model from a trend.
pattern: paying more attention / Therefore, it is vital.
boundary: the trend needs a source if it is a fact.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent the trend.

units.function: credit two models, grant their strength, then say why they are not enough

original_instantiations: Of the models already published, one treats a walker as a chain of states and another uses a force between people. Both are very good at the single person and at the place where movement stops. But a building this large needs a view that runs from the whole down to the part.
Two earlier models handle one walker well and handle a jam well. For a building of many floors that is not enough, because the view has to start at the whole.

units.source_excerpt: Among them, Wakim proposed a Markov pedestrian model; Helbing proposed a social force model. The above models are very suitable for the study of individual movement. However, for a large, multi-story venue, an evacuation model with a general view from the whole to the local is needed.
units.reusable_pattern: Among them, [A] proposed [model]. [B] proposed [model]. The above models are very suitable for [their strength]. However, for [this case], [a different view] is needed.
reusable_elements: occurrences: introduction, second paragraph.
stable function: praise, then outgrow.
pattern: Among them / The above models are very suitable / However, for.
boundary: the gap must be the one this paper fills.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not dismiss the cited models.

units.function: name two causes and the challenge they make

original_instantiations: Because the visitors differ so much and the building is so tangled, safe exit is a real challenge. We need a model that hands the staff a choice of plans.
The mix of visitors and the shape of the building together make a safe exit hard. The model has to give the staff options.

units.source_excerpt: Due to the diversity of visitors and the complex structure of the building, it poses a great challenge to safe evacuation. We need to develop an emergency evacuation model to provide museum staff with options for evacuation options in different situations.
units.reusable_pattern: Due to [cause] and [cause], it poses a great challenge to [the goal]. We need to develop [the model] to provide [who] with options.
reusable_elements: occurrences: restatement, opening.
stable function: two causes, one challenge, one deliverable.
pattern: Due to / it poses a great challenge / options for.
boundary: the doubled word options is a slip; do not copy it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not repeat a noun for emphasis.

units.function: split the task into numbered objectives and then implicit ones

original_instantiations: The model has to do the following. First, give the staff a range of ways out. Second, find the bottlenecks. Third, let the responders in fast. At the same time it should also handle the things not stated outright.
We set the model five jobs, written as a numbered list, and then a second list of jobs the prompt only implies.

units.source_excerpt: The established model needs to accomplish the following objectives: I. Give instructions to allow museum personnel to explore a range of options. At the same time, the model should consider several implicit objectives.
units.reusable_pattern: The established model needs to accomplish the following objectives. At the same time, the model should consider several implicit objectives.
reusable_elements: occurrences: restatement.
stable function: separate what was asked from what was implied.
pattern: needs to accomplish the following / At the same time / implicit.
boundary: mark the implied ones as implied.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present an implied objective as a stated one.

units.function: lay the method out as four numbered steps

original_instantiations: In our program the first step is the small scale, the speed of the flow. The second step builds the graph. The third step is the large scale, where the goal is that every exit runs as fast as it can at each moment. The final step lets the responders in.
We go small, then graph, then large, then responders, and we say so in that order.

units.source_excerpt: In our research program, the first step is the microscopic part. The second step is to establish a spatial node graph. The third step is the macro part: we set the optimization goal as the speed of all exits flow at each moment is the maximum that can be achieved. The final step is to promote the model.
units.reusable_pattern: The first step is [the small]. The second step is [the structure]. The third step is [the large]: we set the optimization goal as [the goal]. The final step is [the extension].
reusable_elements: occurrences: overview.
stable function: four steps, each named by its scale.
pattern: the first step / the second step / the third step / the final step.
boundary: the goal must be the one optimized.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a step that is not done.

units.function: list assumptions as bare numbered sentences with no reasons

original_instantiations: We take five things as given, each on its own line: the signs are clear, most people follow them, nobody falls, nobody walks back against the flow, and the doors are wide enough.
Five assumptions, numbered, no reason attached to any of them.

units.source_excerpt: 1. The guiding signs and notifications of the venues are clear enough. 2. The vast majority of people are rational enough to follow the signs. 4. The crowd will not evacuate in opposite directions.
units.reusable_pattern: Number the assumptions and leave each one as a single sentence.
reusable_elements: occurrences: assumptions.
stable function: a bare list, no justification promised.
pattern: numbered sentences, no because.
boundary: do not add a reason the paper did not give.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the assumptions are justified.

units.function: defer the symbols that do not fit the table

original_instantiations: Anything not in the table gets explained at the point it shows up.
Symbols left out of the table are defined where they are first used.

units.source_excerpt: Note: Symbols not mentioned in the table will be explained if they appear below.
units.reusable_pattern: Note: [items] not mentioned in the table will be explained if they appear below.
reusable_elements: occurrences: notation, footnote.
stable function: keep the table short and promise the rest.
pattern: not mentioned / will be explained if they appear.
boundary: the promise must be kept.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not defer a symbol that is never defined.

units.function: credit a curve, then reject it for being too complex

original_instantiations: An earlier study fitted speed to density from watching aisles and stairs. Sadly, the curve is a messy nonlinear one, and it will not serve over a wide range.
The fitted curve exists, but it is too complicated to use broadly, so we set it aside.

units.source_excerpt: According to the related research of Predtechenski and Milinskii, the average evacuation speed is a function of the flow density. Besides, they used the observation data to fit the relationship curve. Unfortunately, this is a complex nonlinear relationship, that is not suitable for a wide range of applications.
units.reusable_pattern: According to [source], [the relation]. Unfortunately, this is [the defect], that is not suitable for [the use].
reusable_elements: occurrences: speed model, opening.
stable function: cite, then decline.
pattern: According to / Unfortunately / not suitable for.
boundary: the defect must be the reason for the decline.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reject a source without the reason.

units.function: say who simplified the curve and to what

original_instantiations: Later, Nelson and Mowrer cut that relation down to a straight line and picked a different slope for each kind of passage.
The curve was then straightened, with one slope per passage type.

units.source_excerpt: After that, Nelson and Mowrer et al. simplified the relationship between velocity and flow density to a linear relationship, and selected different linear coefficients for different evacuation channels.
units.reusable_pattern: After that, [who] simplified [the relation] to [the simpler form], and selected [the variants].
reusable_elements: occurrences: speed model.
stable function: credit the simplification, not just the source.
pattern: After that / simplified to / selected different.
boundary: name what was simplified.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the simplification as original.

units.function: sum up a model, name where it fails, and announce the search for a replacement

original_instantiations: Put together, this model ties speed to density and gives a stair version and a corridor version, but it fails where the density is high, as at a narrow door. So we look for a better one to take its place.
It covers the open passages and not the tight exit. That is why we go looking for a replacement.

units.source_excerpt: In summary, N&M Model considers the relationship between evacuation speed and flow density, and gives different models for different road sections, but it is not suitable for the situation where the flow density is relatively large. So we try to find a better model to replace it.
units.reusable_pattern: In summary, [the model] [does what], but it is not suitable for [the case]. So we try to find a better model to replace it.
reusable_elements: occurrences: end of 4.1.
stable function: close a model by its gap.
pattern: In summary / but it is not suitable / So we try to find.
boundary: the replacement must follow.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not announce a replacement that never arrives.

units.function: define two quantities in speech and letter them

original_instantiations: Take the exit as the origin. The gap to the person ahead is written as A, and the difference in their speeds as B. The push from the front is then taken as proportional to B over A.
We name the gap A and the relative speed B, and we say the forward drag scales with B divided by A.

units.source_excerpt: The distance from the previous person is |xj - xj-1|, which is recorded as A. The relative velocity is recorded as B. Then the forward damping force caused by crowding is proportional to B/A.
units.reusable_pattern: [The quantity], which is recorded as [a letter]. [The other], which is recorded as [a letter]. Then [the force] is proportional to [the ratio].
reusable_elements: occurrences: front crowding.
stable function: letter a quantity before using it.
pattern: which is recorded as / is proportional to.
boundary: use the letters afterwards.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not letter a quantity and drop it.

units.function: bound where a term applies

original_instantiations: Note that the sideways drag matters only when people are packed tight, and barely matters when they are not.
The side term is for the dense case. At low density it does little.

units.source_excerpt: Note that Side-Crowding is generally suitable when the crowd density is particularly large, and when the population density is small, it has little effect.
units.reusable_pattern: Note that [the term] is generally suitable when [the condition], and when [the other case], it has little effect.
reusable_elements: occurrences: side crowding.
stable function: bound a term in the same sentence.
pattern: Note that / generally suitable when / has little effect.
boundary: both cases must be real.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not bound a term with a guess.

units.function: derive an equation from a named law

original_instantiations: From Newton's second law we wrote down the equation for the escape speed.
The speed equation comes straight from the second law.

units.source_excerpt: According to Newton's second law, we have obtained the following escape velocity dynamics equation.
units.reusable_pattern: According to [the law], we have obtained the following [equation].
reusable_elements: occurrences: before equation (2).
stable function: name the law, then the equation.
pattern: According to / we have obtained the following.
boundary: the equation must follow from the law.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not cite a law the equation does not use.

units.function: state the regime where density stops mattering

original_instantiations: Once the density is low, the speed no longer depends on it, and the critical density does not move the speed either.
Below the critical density the speed is simply constant.

units.source_excerpt: When the density is small, the velocity of the human flow is not affected by it, and the critical density does not affect the velocity.
units.reusable_pattern: When [the quantity] is small, [the result] is not affected by it.
reusable_elements: occurrences: after equation (5).
stable function: name the regime where a term vanishes.
pattern: When / is small / is not affected by it.
boundary: the regime must match the formula.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop a term the formula still uses.

units.function: read a model as three regimes of the same formula

original_instantiations: Read this way, the model is a general one. At high density all three weights stay. As density falls, the front term dominates. Low enough, and only the people's own traits remain, so the speed is just a constant.
One formula, three regimes: all terms, then the front term, then a constant.

units.source_excerpt: It is analyzed that the above model is a generalized model. When the flow density is large, neither of the weights is zero. When the flow density gets smaller, it can be considered to be mainly affected by Front-Crowding; when the flow density is small enough, only the impact of personnel characteristics can be considered, and v is a certain value.
units.reusable_pattern: It is analyzed that the above model is a generalized model. When [high], [all terms]. When [lower], [one term]; when [lowest], [a constant].
reusable_elements: occurrences: after the SES model.
stable function: unpack one formula into regimes.
pattern: It is analyzed that / When / when / when.
boundary: each regime must match the formula.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a regime the formula lacks.

units.function: close a model by naming its one weakness

original_instantiations: The one weakness is that people's traits are vague, so their share of the result cannot be pinned down well.
Its single fault is the fuzzy part, the traits, which the formula cannot really measure.

units.source_excerpt: The only downside is that due to the uncertainty and ambiguity of the characteristics of the personnel, the effect of this part on the whole cannot be well described.
units.reusable_pattern: The only downside is that due to [the cause], [the effect] cannot be well described.
reusable_elements: occurrences: end of the SES model.
stable function: one weakness, named, not a list.
pattern: The only downside is that due to / cannot be well described.
boundary: it must be the real weakness.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call it the only downside if there are more.

units.function: introduce a device as a simplification

original_instantiations: To make the arithmetic easier, we added two made-up nodes.
Two extra nodes were put in so the calculation would be simpler.

units.source_excerpt: To simplify the calculation, we added two hypothetical nodes 1 and 9.
units.reusable_pattern: To simplify the calculation, we added [the device].
reusable_elements: occurrences: graph construction.
stable function: justify an addition by the work it saves.
pattern: To simplify the calculation, we added.
boundary: show the saving later.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a device that saves nothing.

units.function: restate a hard problem as an easy one and say what it now relates

original_instantiations: Adding the two nodes turns a hard many-to-many problem into an easy one-to-one problem. What it now relates is the people still inside to the people leaving.
The problem becomes one start and one end. That links the people left in the rooms to the flow out of the exits.

units.source_excerpt: This creates a new single goal to single goal issue. This result corresponds to the relationship between the total number of people remaining in all rooms and the flow of people leaving all exits. The simplification of the goal brings great convenience to the optimization of the algorithm.
units.reusable_pattern: This creates a new [easy form]. This result corresponds to the relationship between [A] and [B]. The simplification brings great convenience to [the next step].
reusable_elements: occurrences: after the virtual nodes.
stable function: say what the reduction now means.
pattern: This creates / corresponds to the relationship / brings great convenience.
boundary: the correspondence must be exact.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim convenience without the correspondence.

units.function: translate a physical statement into a matrix property

features.transition: from the matrix point of view
original_instantiations: Equal speed both ways means, looked at as a matrix, that the traffic matrix is symmetric, and the diagonal is zero because it means nothing.
Seen as a matrix, the two directions being equal makes it symmetric, and the diagonal is empty on purpose.

units.source_excerpt: From the matrix point of view, this shows that the human traffic matrix is a symmetrical matrix, and the diagonal line is all zero because it has no practical meaning.
units.reusable_pattern: From the matrix point of view, this shows that [the object] is [the property], because [the reason].
reusable_elements: occurrences: corridor matrix.
stable function: give the matrix reading and its reason.
pattern: From the matrix point of view / because.
boundary: the reason must hold.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assert a matrix property without the reason.

units.function: rename the goal as a known problem

original_instantiations: To get people out fastest we have to use every passage as fully as we can at each moment. In this model that is the same as finding the maximum flow from the start to the end at any time.
Fastest exit equals maximum flow from source to sink, and we say so.

units.source_excerpt: In order to get the maximum of escape speed, we need to make full use of the channel resources at any time to maximize the escape rate. In the established model, the problem is equivalent to obtaining the maximum flow from the source to the sink at any time.
units.reusable_pattern: In order to [the goal], we need to [the means]. The problem is equivalent to [the known problem].
reusable_elements: occurrences: before the algorithm.
stable function: rename the goal as a standard problem.
pattern: In order to / the problem is equivalent to.
boundary: the equivalence must be real.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call two problems equivalent loosely.

units.function: invoke a theorem and decline to prove it

original_instantiations: The resulting flow is the maximum, which the max-flow min-cut theorem guarantees. We do not prove that here.
We cite the theorem and say plainly that the proof is not given.

units.source_excerpt: The resulting stream at this point is the maximum flow, which can be proved by the maximum flow minimum cut theorem. And we will not prove this here.
units.reusable_pattern: [The claim], which can be proved by [the theorem]. And we will not prove this here.
reusable_elements: occurrences: end of the algorithm introduction.
stable function: lean on a theorem without pretending to prove it.
pattern: which can be proved by / And we will not prove this here.
boundary: name the theorem.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip a proof silently.

units.function: say the standard method is adapted and name the new one

original_instantiations: Our case is messier than the standard method, so we use it with changes and propose a dynamic planning method built on it.
We keep the known method and change it, and we name what we propose.

units.source_excerpt: Therefore, we properly use the Ford-Fulkerson algorithm in the solution of the problem and propose a dynamic system planning algorithm based on the Ford-Fulkerson algorithm.
units.reusable_pattern: Therefore, we properly use [the method] and propose [the new method] based on it.
reusable_elements: occurrences: algorithm application.
stable function: adaptation, then the new name.
pattern: we properly use / and propose / based on.
boundary: the changes must be stated.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not propose a method that is the original unchanged.

units.function: read a figure as an ordered plan

original_instantiations: Read straight off the figure, the first move is to empty the rooms by the exits, then the rooms behind them feed forward, then a passage may have to split, and at the end the flow falls to nothing.
The figure shows the order: clear the exit rooms, move the next rooms up, split a passage, then let the flow die away.

units.source_excerpt: It can be seen intuitively that the first step of the evacuation plan is to empty the exit rooms. Then the personnel at the second-level nodes move to the adjacent first-level nodes. Then, with the decrease of remaining number, the flow is even reduced to 0, and eventually all evacuation is completed.
units.reusable_pattern: It can be seen intuitively that the first step is [the first]. Then [the next]. Then [the last], and eventually [the end].
reusable_elements: occurrences: evacuation plan.
stable function: turn a figure into a sequence.
pattern: It can be seen intuitively that the first step / Then / eventually.
boundary: the sequence must be in the figure.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not read a step the figure does not show.

units.function: announce a classification before the cases

original_instantiations: We split the bottlenecks into three kinds: a passage that cannot feed its exit, exits placed unevenly, and a single room's door.
Three bottleneck types, named up front, then taken one at a time.

units.source_excerpt: We divide them into three categories: bottlenecks due to channel supply and demand imbalances, bottlenecks due to uneven distribution of exports, and single room export bottlenecks.
units.reusable_pattern: We divide them into [number] categories: [type], [type], and [type].
reusable_elements: occurrences: bottleneck section, opening.
stable function: count, then name.
pattern: We divide them into / categories.
boundary: every named type must be treated.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name a category and skip it.

units.function: name a fix and report that it worked

original_instantiations: To fix it we widen the passage that limits the flow and keep the density the same. The dip goes away and the clearing gets shorter, about 43.2 seconds.
We widen the tight passage. The bottleneck disappears and the time drops.

units.source_excerpt: In order to solve the problem, we choose to expand the width of the restricted channel while keep the density unchanged. It can be seen that the bottleneck is eliminated, as well as evacuation time shortened. The total evacuation time is about 43.2s.
units.reusable_pattern: In order to solve the problem, we choose to [the fix]. It can be seen that [the effect]. The total [result] is [the number].
reusable_elements: occurrences: first bottleneck.
stable function: fix, then the visible effect, then the number.
pattern: In order to solve / we choose to / it can be seen that.
boundary: the number must come from the run.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report a time from a different run.

units.function: offer one case as proof of adaptability

original_instantiations: Take a fire in one room as the example that the model adapts. Only leaving is allowed there, and those people go first. We get both by closing the way in.
One fire, one room, shows the model can change: block the entrance, send the people to the next rooms.

units.source_excerpt: Let's take a fire accident in a room as an example to show that our model is adaptable. Assuming that room 8 is on fire, it should meet such requirements: First, only leaving is allowed. Secondly, people have to be evacuated as soon as possible.
units.reusable_pattern: Let us take [a case] as an example to show that our model is adaptable. It should meet such requirements: First, [one]. Secondly, [two].
reusable_elements: occurrences: adaptive analysis.
stable function: one example stands for adaptability.
pattern: take as an example to show / it should meet such requirements.
boundary: one example is not every threat.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not generalize one fire to all threats.

units.function: offer two options and claim they match practice

original_instantiations: We give two ways. One, watch the flow and let responders in once it falls to 60 or 70 percent of the maximum. Two, when it is urgent, give them one passage and close everything that joins it. Set against real rescues, the plan fits.
Two options: wait for the flow to drop, or hand over one passage at once. We say both match real rescues.

units.source_excerpt: We give two options for this. The first one is real-time monitoring of channel flow. When the flow drops to 60%-70% of the maximum flow, the emergency personnel are allowed to enter. Second, when the situation is particularly urgent, priority is given to emergency personnel. Combined with domestic and foreign rescue cases, our program meets the actual requirements.
units.reusable_pattern: We give two options. The first one is [option]. Second, [option]. Combined with [the check], our program meets the actual requirements.
reusable_elements: occurrences: responder entry.
stable function: two options, then a match to practice.
pattern: We give two options / The first one / Second / meets the actual requirements.
boundary: the match needs a cited case.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim a match to practice without a case.

units.function: turn a run into three timed conclusions

original_instantiations: From the run we draw three things. Early on, keep the exits clear. In the middle, the far rooms jam, so open exits nearer them. Late, some passages have gone quiet, so let the responders in.
Three stages, three actions: open exits, add exits for the far rooms, then admit responders.

units.source_excerpt: From the simulation, we can summarize the following conclusions: I. At the beginning, keep the exit area open. II. In the middle, the rooms far away from the exit are very congested, so consider opening other exits. III. In the later stage, the flow of some channels has been reduced, allowing rescuers to enter.

Six instructions, each one something the staff does with the model.

units.source_excerpt: In order to give museum personnel a complete model exploration method, we give the following suggestions: perfect the model, set up a density detector, once the accident occurs the model is quickly used, adjust the model based on actual accidents, arrange the extra exits, find the most appropriate route and time for rescuers.

It generalizes because nothing in it is special to one building, and a change is easy to make.
